title: Shot multiplexing lab docket
content:
Purpose:
Short log of experiments exploring 'shot multiplexing' — combining heterogeneous few-shot exemplars into compact templates that adapt by role/intent. Goal is to find framing patterns that reduce hallucinations for product Q&A while keeping token budgets under 120 tokens for the template header.

Hypotheses to test (rough):
- H1: Interleaving 2 compact task examples + 1 persona example yields better factual recall than 3 homogeneous task examples when prompts include explicit retrieval hints.
- H2: Labelled exemplar borders (---EXAMPLE N---) reduce model overgeneralization in multi-domain fewshot sets.
- H3: Short meta-instructions (8–12 words) placed AFTER exemplars are more stable than before for models with context window 2048.

Design notes / constraints:
- Keep exemplar size <= 40 tokens each where possible.
- Avoid long role descriptions; prefer single-token role tags (e.g., [AGENT], [USER]) but test one variant with 1-sentence persona.
- Token budget for header+shots <= 120 tokens. Target final prompt total <= 512 when paired with user query.

Experiment matrix (quick):
- Variant A: 3 like-task shots, no persona, meta-instr before shots.
- Variant B: 2 task shots + 1 persona shot, persona last, meta-instr after shots.
- Variant C: same as B but with explicit delimiter lines + labelled headers.
- Variant D: B + retrieval hint ("If unsure, say: I don't know; suggest source query").

Example templates (compact):
- B (baseline compact):
  "You are a product help assistant. Examples:
  [EX1] Q: How can I export logs? A: Use Settings > Export > choose timeframe.
  [EX2] Q: My API times out at 30s; why? A: Increase timeout config or use batching; see docs/timeout.
  [PERSONA] Agent: concise, cite steps, offer next action.
  Answer concisely:"

- C (labelled delim):
  "---EXAMPLE 1---
  Q: How to rotate an API key?
  A: In Console > Keys > Rotate; update all clients.
  ---EXAMPLE 2---
  Q: Where are usage charges shown?
  A: Billing > Usage breakdown per model.
  ---AGENT PERSONA---
  \"Agent: Ask clarifying Q if missing context; include link when appropriate.\""

Failure cases observed (notes/log):
- Soft hallucination: model invents a console path that exists only in internal staging when exemplars include nonstandard button names. Repro recipe: Variant A + user query "Where is X in the console?" -> model says "Settings > Advanced > X" (no such page).
- Overfitting to examples: repeating example phrasing as answer verbatim even when user asks for a different scope. E.g., example uses timeframe 'last 7 days' and model defaults to that phrase for unrelated queries.
- Persona bleed: when persona contains explicit instructions to ask clarifying questions, the model sometimes only asks questions and avoids answering even when query is direct.

Mitigations to try:
- Replace concrete path names in examples with templated tokens like <CONSOLE_PATH> to avoid anchoring to staging labels.
- Add negative exemplar: short shot that demonstrates 'I don't know' behavior to lower hallucination confidence. Example: Q: "Is feature Y available?" A: "I don't know; check Feature Flags > Y or ask platform-admin."
- Use explicit guard: "If the model is not >80% confident, respond: 'I don't know; suggest doc search'" (test whether model respects conditional confidence phrasing).

Metrics / evaluation plan:
- Primary: factual accuracy on a 50-item curated checklist (binary).
- Secondary: hallucination severity score (0–3) per response.
- Tertiary: concision (tokens in reply) and user-satisfaction proxy from annotation (1–5).
- Track per-model and per-temperature (0.0, 0.3, 0.7).

Quick test log (2025-01-20):
- Model: open-model-2048-v1, temp 0.0, Variant C. Results: 50 items: accuracy 0.68, hallucination mean 1.1. Not great but better than A (0.52).
- Notes: delimited headers reduced spurious concatenation of examples (fewer answer mashups).

Edge cases to add to bench:
- Partial info queries (missing key id, ambiguous resource name).
- Nonstandard locale phrasing (UK vs US English UI labels).
- Rate-limit/burst error messages — ensure the assistant doesn't suggest making more requests when rate-limited.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q1: How does shot ordering interact with retrieval hints? Need a 2x2 run: (ordering: persona-last/persona-first) x (retrieval-hint: on/off).
- Q2: Can we compress two task examples into a single composite example without losing signal? Try joining by semicolon.
- Q3: Is explicit negative exemplar more effective than a policy sentence like "Do not hallucinate"?

Next steps (immediate):
- Run ordered 2x2 for Q1 (Linear ticket PL-482 assigned).
- Prototype negative exemplar vs policy sentence with 100-shot bootstrap.
- Share a short writeup for Solutions team with 3 best templates (week of 2025-02-10).

References and links:
- Linear ticket: PL-482 (shot multiplexing experiments).
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-tools/pull/78 — small harness for automated few-shot runs.
- Slack thread: #prompt-sandbox (see pinned message Jan 14).

Notes to self: keep living examples small. When in doubt, add a retrieval hint. If persona causes over-questioning, swap to micro-tag only (e.g., [AGENT-CONCISE]).

Scratchpad snippets to paste into harness quickly:
- Compact example 1: \"Q: How to enable dedicated capacity? A: Contact sales@redwood; set up Dedicated in Console > Capacity.\"
- Negative exemplar: \"Q: Is model X compliant with GDPR? A: I don't know; check compliance docs or ask security@redwood.\"

End of docket.

(Free-form: I want to try a mini A/B where we put the meta-instruction as a suffix token only: "Respond: <policy>" — quick hack but maybe useful.)
